principle: Meaning first, image generation second. Scene and canonical mapping audit precede the art brief; reference illustrations inform visual language only.

prompts.dungeonSemanticPrompt:
Create an ORIGINAL professional 2D OSR adventure-module dungeon illustration for an interactive reference map, landscape 760:620 ratio. The three attached images are ONLY general print-map style/palette references, not layouts to copy. Do not imitate their exact maps or an artist. No sketch is supplied: construct the image from this semantic room brief.

MEANING FIRST: A person enters from the SOUTH, can inspect a furnished room and its open eastern alcove, and can leave through a NORTH exit reached by a short passage. This is one contiguous place, not an arrangement of icons. Draw a clear connected room plan, top-down with consistent near-orthographic objects and deliberate ink work. Main chamber roughly x25–80%, y28–72%; a short southern approach and stone entrance arch centered x50%,y82%; a narrow northern passage and stairs lead to an unmistakable exit at x50%,y8%. The eastern lower alcove is a broad continuous extension of the SAME ROOM: no dividing wall, door, threshold or detached cave bubble. It can have rough darker teal stone at its outer edge. Leave about 12% height BELOW the southern arch for exterior ground and approach clues.

Canonical meanings to make visible:
• Architecture: continuous irregular coral masonry, with one genuinely crumbled part on the west side. Clear flagstone floor itself communicates room shape; NO separate rolled parchment or arbitrary slab pretending to be the room shape.
• Discovery: a small square wooden table at left-center, with a journal fragment on its top. Four legs sit directly beneath the four corners, subtle and physically correct, not spikes protruding sideways.
• Room contents: modest clay pots and a little abandoned cloth in upper-middle.
• Loot: a SMALL ochre wooden chest tucked against northeast wall, about 5–6% of image width, not dominating the room.
• Trap: one suspicious partly depressed/lifted paving stone INSET INTO THE FLOOR in the southern approach just INSIDE the entrance, around x50%,y74%. It belongs to the walking route, no floating trap platform, no exposed row of decorative yellow triangles.
• Remains / room dressing: a SMALL scattered cluster of ANIMAL BONES in the eastern open alcove around x81%,y63%, no human skeleton. Long-snouted goat-like skull and a few ribs/bones, all solid pale IVORY with dark outlines, contrasting clearly with the darker floor; entire cluster no more than 7% of image width. No money pouch.
• Light: one modest lit wall sconce at northwest, correctly attached to wall.
• Room air / smell: subtle low pale haze close to the southwestern interior floor, no bowl, nose, flame-shaped smell icon, or specific source.
• Entrance smell: a separate shallow layer of mist hugging the GROUND outside the southern arch and across its threshold. Mist does NOT issue from a wall or rock.
• Sound: just THREE small, elegant cream sound-wave arcs in the empty upper-right margin, as restrained sensory notation. No ear, no speaker, no protruding brick, no source invented.
• Entrance state: a few fallen masonry fragments BELOW the entrance, outside on lower-left approach around x37%,y95%.
• Entrance signs: a few scuffs/drag traces and a torn cloth scrap BELOW the entrance on lower-right approach around x63%,y95%.

Visual direction: strong spatial silhouettes and plausible scale, irregular fitted masonry and flagstones, authored engraving/woodcut line weights, subtle cheap-offset print grain. Palette: charcoal #292727 ground, pale green #bdc69b flagstones, coral #bb786b masonry, ivory #ece6b8 bones and details, muted teal #658880 alcove, sparse ochre #e3d477 props. Rough print quality with PROFESSIONAL drawing and precise composition. Keep negative space, never fill it with meaningless random hatch strokes. No text, labels, numbers, lettering, logo, UI, cards, buttons, border, watermark, glossy 3D or gradients. All objects should be believable parts of this room; sensory notation stays modest.
prompts.journeySemanticPrompt:
Create an ORIGINAL professional illustrated OSR wilderness JOURNEY MAP for an interactive reference desk, landscape aspect 760:620. The supplied three pictures are style-only examples of printed adventure-module maps, NOT compositions to copy. Use NO earlier sketches or generated scene as a layout. Build a physically coherent place from the semantic brief below.

Consistent TOP-DOWN ORTHOGRAPHIC plan view throughout: terrain, buildings, bridge, camp and props. Old-school ink and flat limited print color, not a 3D landscape or a collection of isolated menu icons.

GEOGRAPHY AND ROUTE: A river runs from the upper edge around x62% to the bottom edge around x56%, meandering gently down the right-middle of the page. The stream has two clear banks and blue water continuously beneath a bridge. A dirt road leaves a small village in the upper-left, winds toward the river, crosses it ONCE around y39%, then continues on the east bank toward the lower-right edge. At the crossing the RIVER runs vertically and the ROAD runs horizontally. A SHORT timber bridge runs LEFT–RIGHT across WATER ONLY, connecting the two banks. Its deck fits just between the bank abutments; road approaches meet the short deck ends exactly. Do not place the bridge diagonally along the river, on top of a road segment, or with a road turning beneath it. Top-down planks, two parallel rails along the long edges; no perspective ambiguity. No second crossing or ford.

MEANINGFUL DISCOVERY FEATURES, each distinct and believable:
• Village: a small connected walled hamlet with several top-down roofs at upper-left x20%,y19%; gate opens to the road.
• Distance marker: a worn roadside milestone/cairn along the approach around x44%,y24%, blank incised tally marks, no words.
• Water landmark: natural river bend with reed bed and exposed rocks upstream of the bridge around x64%,y22%, part of the river.
• Signs of travelers: ordinary BOOTPRINTS and a little worn track on the west road approach around x43%,y43%.
• Threat signs: at forest edge around x31%,y44%, a standing/truncated tree trunk DEEPLY GOUGED by large claws, freshly snapped branches and disturbed brush. It must visibly suggest something dangerous passed; NOT a neatly sawn lumber log, not the same bootprints as travelers.
• Foraging: identifiable small berry/herb cluster in a clearing on the left forest edge around x18%,y62%. Connected canopy mass behind it, realistic varied trees.
• Leaving the road: a narrow footpath branches from the western approach and disappears into the lower-left trees; it is a genuine side route.
• Campsite: a modest camp on dry east-bank ground around x81%,y63%, set back from water. A small correctly constructed canvas A-FRAME TENT viewed FROM ABOVE: a straight roof ridge with TWO coherent canvas roof slopes, guy ropes to four ground pegs, a little doorway at ONE short end. No contradictory front/side perspective; no impossible black roof plane. Light comes from upper-left everywhere: tent's upper-left-facing slope cream, opposite slope restrained peach shade, cast shadow to lower-right. A small stone-ring campfire beside the tent, never merged into the fabric.
• Remains: a SMALL scattered deer/goat animal skull and a few ribs near the east river bank around x82%,y45%, IVORY filled bones with dark outlines, no giant human skeleton; cluster at most 5–6% of map width.
• Roadside event: an abandoned damaged handcart and spilled bundle on the far right road margin around x88%,y83%, a plausible incident to inspect.
• Weather: restrained small engraved raincloud in the upper-right open map margin, no face, no text.

Palette derived generally from supplied reference 3: gray-green printed ground, mustard/olive forest, muted dark slate-blue river, warm salmon dirt road and roof accents, ivory canvas/bones, charcoal ink. Professional composition: connected geography, clear scale relationships, expressive specific silhouettes; fine print grain and controlled engraving only where it describes actual material. Do not cover empty space with arbitrary scratches. No labels, letters, numbers, UI, cards, buttons, decorative compass, border, watermark, glossy game art or gradients. Keep map landmarks usable at a small display size.
prompts.citySemanticPrompt:
Create an ORIGINAL professional 2D OSR CITY CRAWL map illustration, 760:620 landscape ratio. Attached images are ONLY general print-map visual references, never copy their artwork/composition. Construct the map from the actual navigation meanings in this brief, not from any sketch or earlier scene.

A physically coherent small town fragment, consistent top-down / very shallow module cutaway view, dense connected building plots and visible streets. North city gate connects to one main cobbled street, which reaches a modest gathering plaza then branches toward market and residential lanes. Buildings face and can be entered from these streets. Color palette inspired generally by reference 2: charcoal plum ground, lavender stone walls and roofs, muted teal streets and courtyard floor, dusty rose market awning/signs, ivory highlights. Professional authored engraved linework and restrained offset-print grain, no random decorative scratches.

Each feature has an exact meaning:
1 Gate reaction: north gate x47%,y15% with TWO small guards standing at its threshold; gate is an actual boundary between outside and town.
2 Signs before entering: posted papers and worn cloth banner on OUTSIDE face of wall beside gate x31%,y12%; no readable words.
3 Street: continuous connected teal cobblestone main road from gate down middle and branches to both sides; sensible width, intersections, curbs.
4 Street surface: distinct patch of uneven/repaired cobbles in lower-center road around x48%,y85%.
5 Street hazard: rubble from an unstable balcony/scaffold in a narrow alley between northeast plots at x65%,y42%; clearly a physical street hazard, no huge symbolic black star-shaped pit.
6 Neighborhood smell: an actual small CHIMNEY on a northeast building around x85%,y23% with a few restrained ink smoke traces; no smoke rising from a random city-wall brick.
7 Gatherings: five or six small top-down human silhouettes gathered in the central plaza x47%,y55%, physically at human scale, not floating heads or board-game tokens.
8 Tavern: southwest building x23%,y65%, recognizable by a SMALL hanging tankard sign and a door facing the street, roof and perimeter structurally coherent.
9 Businesses: southeast shop x77%,y83%, shuttered storefront and goods at doorway; reachable by branch street.
10 Townhouse interior: northeast enclosed house/courtyard block x80%,y32%, a small cutaway glimpse of interior or courtyard at entrance; same roof grammar as other buildings.
11 Pray: modest upper-left open/cutaway shrine x19%,y30%, altar visible inside, entered from west branch street.
12 Merchant disposition: market stall with dusty-rose canvas canopy, goods, and one small vendor silhouette on middle-right street x73%,y59%, separate from permanent shop.
13 Directions: a weathered two-arm signpost at lower main-street fork around x38%,y81%; blank signs, no text.

Use pictographic place-making: masonry, roofs, paving, entrances, props occupy actual space and share scale. No unnecessary wells/pits resembling extra interactive controls, no isolated icon grid. No modern UI, text, labels, letters, numbers, cards, buttons, decorative frame, watermark, glossy 3D or photographic effects. Keep all 13 semantic features recognizable on a small screen.
prompts.dungeonRefinementPrompt:

Preserve the contiguous room, small ivory ANIMAL bones, north exit, south entrance, journal table, pots, chest, inset approach trap, colors, print line quality and all other positions. Make ONLY these five corrections, considering physical room context:
1 The flame around x27%,y25% must be a small WALL-MOUNTED SCONCE attached directly to the northwest INNER MASONRY FACE with a visible short iron bracket. It is not standing on the floor and has no little floor legs. Match the map's perspective.
2 Remove the large clean smooth wave logo at x90%,y9%. Redraw three much SMALLER imperfect ink sound-wave arcs immediately beside the northeast wall around x75%,y21%, close to the dungeon silhouette. They are restrained rough printed sensory notation, not a polished logo. No ear and no protruding wall brick.
3 Interior low mist around x29%,y62% must be represented as flat engraved cream ink: a few shallow broken horizontal curling bands and stipple/hatching, sharp-edged print marks. NO realistic translucent smoke, blur, airbrush, bloom or gradient.
4 Entrance low mist around x47%,y84% must use the SAME flat engraved low-mist treatment, hugging the threshold ground. It does NOT emerge from the wall. Keep threshold visible through breaks in the printed bands.
5 The south entrance must connect coherently to outside: carry the corridor's flagstones through a clear stone threshold into a SHORT PAVED APPROACH immediately outside, then meet the dirt/scuff ground with a deliberate clear edge. Keep the same top-down/low-cutaway map perspective, no abruptly changing plane or blurry blended transition. Keep fallen stones and cloth/drag marks BELOW the entrance on this outside approach. Do not add more paths or gates.
No text, labels, watermark or new unrelated objects. Preserve original illustration dimensions and professional OSR print style.

This map has one coherent landscape scale; the cart, campsite and trees determine it. No text, no labels, no new objects, no new paths, no layout changes.
